messages:
ravi: heads-up — saw another spike in eu-west yesterday where CA kept provisioning cheap spot gpu nodes and we tripped egress quotas + network HT throttles. app latency jumped for a few minutes. wondering if we should add a surge-safety/window or regional fallback to avoid mass-provisioning into a single AZ :thinking:

emily: ugh. do we have the debug logs from the CA pod? was it expanding multiple nodegroups or repeatedly scaling the same group?

ravi: CA logs show repeated scale-ups for nodegroup-gpu-spot-eu1, then scale-downs failed due to pods with local storage + long PDBs. expander=price was choosing cheap nodes; request distribution concentrated in that AZ.

kai: price expander makes sense cost-wise but risky for AZ skew. couple quick thoughts: 1) add --balance-similar-node-groups to keep expansion balanced across nodegroups, 2) set --expander=priority and give higher priority to diverse AZ nodegroups, or 3) implement a short surge window to rate-limit back-to-back scale-ups.

sophie: +1 for a surge window. we hit our network quota when CA spun 8 nodes in 3 minutes. a simple circuit-breaker would help. also we should lower --max-node-provision-time so we don't wait forever for unhealthy instances.

emily: what's the exact flag list we want to try in staging? could we also use taints to prefer on-demand for sensitive workloads?

kai: proposed CA args (staging patch):
```
--expander=priority \n--balance-similar-node-groups=true \n--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m \n--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 \n--max-node-provision-time=10m \n--node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled,kubernetes.io/role=gpu \n--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false \n--ok-total-unready-count=3 \n--ok-total-unready-percent=10 \n```
We can also add a lightweight rate limiter outside CA using a controller that blocks >3 concurrent scale-up events per region (short-term).

ravi: I like priority expander + balance flag. for priority we need to annotate nodegroups with autoscaler-priority: high/medium/low. do we have tooling to automate that?

sophie: yes, we can add labels in nodepool templates. example: 
`autoscaler.k8s.io/priority: "100"` for on-demand, `"10"` for spot. CA priority expander reads that. we'll add a simple smoke test in staging to ensure it chooses different pools.

emily: about the surge/circuit-breaker — we could implement a temporal lock in the CA deployment: if more than N scale-ups happen in T seconds in a region, pause further expansion for M minutes and route new requests to fallback on-demand pools. autoscaler-bot can post alerts when the lock is engaged.

autoscaler-bot: [automated] Surge lock engaged for eu-west: 4 scale-ups in 120s. Pausing spot expansions for 5m. Reason: network egress exceed threshold.

kai: perfect — can we make that lock configurable via configmap so SRE can tweak thresholds without redeploy? also add a prometheus metric `ca_surge_lock_state{region}`.

ravi: agreed. metric + configmap + bot alerting. let's run this in staging for 48h and monitor: P95 latency, number of scale-ups, egress usage, and scale-down failures.

emily: I'll open a small PR with the CA args + the surge-lock controller scaffold and a kustomize overlay for staging. tagging @sophie for the nodepool label changes.

sophie: got it. i'll prep nodepool templates and add a short note to docs about priorities and fallback behavior. also will add a preflight check: if region egress usage > 80% do not allow spot expansions.

ravi: timeline? if we can test next week we can roll to prod end of week. keep the threshold conservative at first.

emily: PR: https://git.internal/repo/infra/ca/commit/ab12cd — contains flags and a basic surge-lock controller (staging only). please review.

kai: reviewing now. small nit — change `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` to 0.45 for GPU workloads (they tend to be bursty).

sophie: noted. i'll update nodepool labels and put a canary in eu-west-1 with on-demand fallback.

ravi: thanks team. post-mortem note: next time this happens, mark timeline + which nodegroups CA targeted so we can refine priorities. adding to incidents channel as well. :thumbsup:
